samples.summary: New "refuse to record baselines from fallback glyphs" gate is bypassable in exactly the scenario it names (fonts.googleapis.com unreachable)
samples.evidence: The delta adds an integrity gate (lines 627-645) that fails the run and refuses `visual:update` when webfonts never became usable. What feeds that gate is `waitForFontsReady`, and the set it waits on is derived *entirely* from `document.fonts` (`registry()`, line 385-396). If the Google Fonts CSS `<link>` in packages/frontend/index.html:10-13 (and the lazily injected per-family links from font-catalog.ts:158-162) never loads — DNS blocked, egress-less Docker network, proxy 403 — the CSS is never parsed, so *zero* `@font-face` rules are registered. `registry()` then returns a map with no Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains-Mono entry, `pending()` (line 415-439) iterates nothing, returns `[]`, and line 480 declares the pass settled. `webFontFailures` stays empty, so the gate at line 640 (`Refusing to record baselines from fallback glyphs`) never fires and the run happily writes 220 baselines painted in the browser's default serif — or, in compare mode, reports pixel diffs with no hint that fonts were the cause. This is the same vacuous-truth flaw the task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:47-52) says it is fixing, moved one level up from `fonts.check()` to the registry itself: a face that was never registered is indistinguishable from a page with no web fonts. The gate reads as covered against a hostile/blocked CDN but is not; nothing asserts that the families the app is known to request (or that at least one `link[href^=https://fonts.googleapis.com/]` actually resolved) are present in the registry at all.

samples.summary: DOM-derived font family names are interpolated unescaped into a CSS font shorthand passed to fonts.check()/fonts.load()
samples.evidence: `unquote()` (line 381) strips only a single leading/trailing quote and performs no escaping, and the result is spliced straight into a CSS font shorthand: `document.fonts.load(`${weight} 12px "${family}"`)` (line 409) and `document.fonts.check(`${weight} 12px "${family}"`)` (line 430). The family string comes from whatever `@font-face` rules the page has registered — for the harness that is third-party CSS fetched live from fonts.googleapis.com plus any app-injected per-family link built from a document-supplied family name (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:151-162 accepts an arbitrary `family: string`). A family containing `"` or `\` breaks out of the quoted string and either silently changes which font descriptor is queried or makes `fonts.check()` throw a synchronous SyntaxError, which rejects the `page.evaluate` and aborts the whole capture. `load()`'s rejection is swallowed at line 409, so only `check()` surfaces it. CSS.escape/`JSON.stringify` on the family (or matching the FontFace object directly instead of re-querying by string) would remove the interpolation entirely. I could not demonstrate an attacker-controlled family reaching this script in CI, hence low confidence.

samples.summary: Origin check on the refetch target uses a string prefix match on link.href rather than a parsed origin comparison
samples.evidence: `refetchPass` selects the stylesheets it will re-point with `link.href.startsWith("https://fonts.googleapis.com/")` (line 464-466) and then rewrites `link.href` (line 470). The trailing slash happens to defeat the obvious `https://fonts.googleapis.com.evil.test/` suffix trick, and the harness page is local, so I could not construct a live bypass. But this is the string-prefix-origin-check antipattern: it is one dropped slash away from matching a lookalike host, and the safe form is already available two lines down — `new URL(link.href).origin === "https://fonts.googleapis.com"`. Worth tightening while the code is being written rather than after it is copied to a page whose links are less trusted.

verdict.reason: The described mechanism is factually real: registry() (verify-visual-browser.mjs:385-396) derives the awaited set solely from document.fonts, pending() (:415-439) returns [] for an empty map, :480 declares the pass settled, and the gate at :627-645 keys only on webFontFailures.length, so a never-loaded Google Fonts CSS (index.html:10-13) leaves the 'Refusing to record baselines from fallback glyphs' check vacuous. But it is not blocking under the Security rubric. This file is a dev/CI visual-regression harness (local Vite server + Playwright writing PNG baselines into tests/visual/baselines); it is not a production code path and handles no untrusted input. The gate at :640 is not an authorization/permission gate - no roles, resource ownership, or IDOR surface; there is no secret, no injection sink, no signature/HMAC or constant-time comparison, no unsafe deserialization, and no SSRF (the refetch at :463-473 only appends a cache-busting param to the app's own hardcoded https://fonts.googleapis.com/ hrefs, which are not attacker-influenced). The worst outcome is baselines recorded with fallback glyphs, i.e. a test-integrity/correctness defect explicitly deferred by this lens ('General logic bugs (correctness lens) ... test quality'). A blocked CDN is an environment/availability condition, not a crossed trust boundary. Refuted as out-of-scope for the Security lens rather than as non-existent - the correctness reviewer should own it.
